Diverges in BOTH directions with concrete trigger bytes: (A) valid RH3+UDP checksummed over final dst -\u003e Rust Rule255 Ok, Python fatal 'invalid Rule 255 IPv6 UDP checksum' (Rust-encoded in-transit datagram fatally rejected by Python); (B) Routing type 0 (forbidden class, RFC 5095) with segments_left=1 and outer-dst checksum -\u003e Python Rule255 accepted and forwarded, Rust fatal 'unsupported RPL source-routing header'. Same wire bytes get opposite verdicts on both encode and decode. new_value: Fixed and pinned. Canonical policy = RH3-only routing headers (RFC 6554: type 3, CmprI/CmprE/Pad octets zero, full 128-bit addresses, segments_left <= address_count; RFC 5095 type 0 rejected) + RFC 2460 s8.1 UDP checksum scope (final RH3 address while segments_left != 0, else outer dst). Changes: (1) Python validate_full_ipv6 gains _validate_routing_headers (headers.py) mirroring Rust codec.rs:281-328 exactly (index mapping, 24-byte floor, address_count floor-division, last-address slice, last-RH3-wins, Fragment rejection via parser, checksum over returned upper-layer dst). (2) C validate_ipv6_header_chain added in schc_helpers.c + IPV6_NH_*/IPV6_ROUTING_TYPE_RPL_SRH constants in schc_internal.h, called from validate_ipv6_transport_lengths — required so the shared vectors hold C parity. (3) Rust production code unchanged (was already canonical); added tests srh_packet/routing_header_policy_matches_rfc6554_and_rfc2460/fragment_header_is_unsupported. (4) 4 shared vectors in schc_compression.json after rpl_dao_no_dodagid_nonmatch: srh3_in_transit_udp_fallback (fallback), routing_type0_malformed, srh3_segments_left_overflow_malformed, ipv6_fragment_header_malformed — hex built with an independent RFC 1071 checksum oracle (no lichen code), then byte-verified by a reviewer's own implementation. Gates: python tests/schc + test_vectors + relay vectors 2170 passed (incl 5 new header tests), vector tooling 57 passed; rust lib 78 passed, shared_vectors 3 passed (44 vectors); C parity scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py PASS across Python+Rust+C (ASan/UBSan); ruff, mypy, clippy, cppcheck, cargo fmt clean. 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness, all empirical) found no defect in the changed Python/C/Rust logic or vectors; all confirmed findings are adjacent pre-existing gaps filed as new beads discovered-from this one: worker6-hahk (P1 C compress gate skips UDP checks for ext-header packets + no checksum on Rule255 fallback), worker6-lqgt (P2 C Rule255 decompress validates nothing), worker6-xyix (P1 Rust/Python routers deliver in-transit RH3 locally where C forwards per RFC 6554), worker6-nyx7 (P3 C latent OOB read guard). The Python-vs-Rust address-policy laxness already tracked as worker6-k0r2 (no duplicate filed). Note: C checksum non-enforcement is NOT a regression of this bead's Python<->Rust alignment; it is the pre-existing broader C-gate gap in worker6-hahk.
